title: What Happened to Us?
content:
Shreya answered the call with a smile.

"Hello?"

A familiar voice came from the other end.

"Shreya..."

The moment she recognized the voice, her smile grew even brighter.

"Siddu!"

"What happened to you?"

"Ever since you went to India, you've completely disappeared."

"No calls..."

"No messages..."

"Were you really that busy?"

Siddu let out a soft laugh.

"Actually..."

"I've been busy helping a friend with his love story."

"So, I couldn't call you."

Shreya smiled warmly.

"Really?"

"Then tell me..."

"Did everything go well?"

A satisfied smile appeared on Siddu's face.

"Yes."

"That's exactly why I called."

"My friend is getting married."

"And his father insisted that I invite all my friends."

"So..."

"You have to come to the wedding."

Shreya's face instantly brightened.

"Is that so?"

"Then please congratulate him on my behalf."

"And don't worry..."

"I'll definitely come."

Siddu smiled.

"I knew you'd say that."

"I'll call you again with all the details later."

"Bye, Shreya."

She smiled warmly.

"Bye, Siddu."

The call ended.

Shreya gently placed her phone back on the table.

A smile still lingered on her face.

Yagnesh looked at her curiously.

"Everything okay?"

She nodded.

"Yes."

"A friend of mine is getting married."

"He just invited me."

Yagnesh smiled.

"Looks like we'll be attending a wedding soon."

Shreya looked at him with a playful smile.

"I guess we will."

________________________________________

Meanwhile...

Back in Shimla...

Siddu had barely slipped his phone into his pocket when Yashwanth walked into the room.

A mischievous smile appeared on his face.

"What are you doing?"

Siddu leaned back comfortably.

"I'm inviting my friends to your wedding."

Yashwanth chuckled.

"Oh?"

"Whom did you call just now?"

Siddu replied casually.

"Shreya."

The smile on Yashwanth's face instantly disappeared.

"What?"

"You mean..."

"You're still talking to Shreya?"

Siddu nodded calmly.

"Yes."

"When did that happen?"

Yashwanth asked in complete surprise.

"I thought both of you had completely lost contact."

A faint smile appeared on Siddu's face.

"It's a long story."

Patiently...

He told Yashwanth everything.

From the unexpected day he and Shreya met again...

To every misunderstanding...

Every painful truth...

And everything that had happened afterward.

Yashwanth listened without interrupting.

When Siddu finally finished...

He let out a deep sigh.

"So..."

"Everything ended well after all."

Then, a teasing smile slowly appeared on his face.

"By the way..."

"When are you and Sneha getting married?"

Siddu looked at him in confusion.

"Who?"

"You and Sneha."

Yashwanth replied as though it were the most obvious thing in the world.

Siddu couldn't help but laugh.

"Looks like no one told you what happened."

Yashwanth folded his arms.

"And who exactly was there to tell me?"

"I've been busy with my own problems."

The smile on Siddu's face slowly faded.

For a brief moment...

Silence filled the room.

Then...

Taking a deep breath...

He slowly began telling Yashwanth everything.

He spoke about Sneha...

About the misunderstandings that had separated them...

About the pain they had silently carried...

And about how fate had changed both of their lives.

When he finished...

Yashwanth remained completely silent.

He stared at Siddu for several long moments.

"So..."

"So much happened behind my back..."

"And you never even thought of telling me?"

There was disappointment in his voice.

"I thought we never hid anything from each other."

Siddu lowered his eyes.

"It's not like that, Yash."

"I just..."

"I wasn't in the right state of mind to talk about it."

He slowly looked up.

A faint smile appeared on his face.

"If I had forgotten our friendship..."

"Then why would I have come all the way from France just for you?"

Yashwanth looked into his friend's eyes.

For a few moments...

He didn't say a single word.

Neither of them spoke again.

Some wounds didn't need advice...

They only needed someone willing to understand them.

And in that quiet silence...

Yashwanth finally realized how much pain his best friend had been carrying all this time.
